label: early-prefix combo: (x/g/w/2/e/t/m)... then g/w/2, then p/e/a/u/t or <DEL> at step 2-4
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.01% of steps) that fires only at steps 2-4, nearly always on the 3rd/4th original input, or on <DEL> when L=3/4. It fires on a specific combination of tokens: the previous input is g, w or 2 (prev_tok lift 12-16x); the earlier prefix is made of tokens from {x,g,w,2,e,t,m}, with first token x the strongest (13x lift); and the current input is p (11.6x, 35% of mass), e, a, u or t, or <DEL>. Magnitude is largest for x g w p, x g g p, x g 2 p and x g w <DEL>. Prefixes starting with t/w/m/e give the weaker activations. It essentially never fires in the copy phase (1% of mass) or at t<2 or t>4. The description is incomplete: the broad version (prev g/w/2 at t=2-4, current p/e/a/u/t/<DEL>) covers about 82% of mass at only about 4% precision. Requiring the whole prefix to come from the set raises precision to about 14%, at about 57% recall. Many steps that match the pattern stay silent, e.g. h o g a and q w g p, so the exact token conjunction that drives it is not captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=w (+3.81), prev_tok=2 (+3.80), prev2_tok=g (+3.80), orig0=x (+3.13), prev3_tok=x (+3.09), prev2_tok=e (+3.02). Lower it: correct=1 (-7.11), in_first=0 (-0.55).
